title: Sell Mineral Rights in Eunice, NM
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Eunice, NM | Royalty Buyer
metaDescription: Eunice, NM sits in Lea County's active Delaware Basin acreage near the Texas line. Get a candid cash offer from a former operations engineer.
heroLead: Eunice sits almost on the Texas line, close enough that a lot of the oilfield traffic through town doesn't stop to think which state it's in.
intro: Lea County has been one of the most heavily developed counties in the New Mexico side of the Delaware Basin, and Eunice sits within that activity directly, close to both the state line and to a substantial amount of recent horizontal drilling. If your family holds minerals near Eunice, this is genuinely productive ground, not a marginal corner of the play.

sections.heading: Border-town position, real drilling density
paragraphs: Lea County's proximity to Texas means a lot of the same operators active in Gaines and Andrews counties on the Texas side also run programs right across the line near Eunice, and the geology doesn't change much crossing that boundary.

sections.heading: New Mexico factors to keep in mind
paragraphs: Surface ownership near Eunice can include state trust or federal land, which affects permitting pace differently than a purely private Texas lease. I ask about this specifically before finalizing your number.

sections.heading: What gets you a fast, honest answer
paragraphs: A division order or recent check stub is the quickest path. Given how active Lea County has been, even modest fractional interests near Eunice tend to carry real value.

sections.heading: Closing from anywhere
paragraphs: Most owners I work with near Eunice live outside New Mexico entirely, and the process accounts for that from the start. I confirm title, send documents by mail or courier, and most clean-title closings run three to six weeks from a signed agreement. Long distance has never been a real obstacle for any seller I've worked with here.

faqs.question: Is Lea County as active as the Texas counties nearby?
faqs.answer: Yes, it's been one of the more heavily drilled counties on the New Mexico side of the Delaware Basin, with development that mirrors what's happening just across the state line.

faqs.question: Does it matter that Eunice is so close to the Texas border?
faqs.answer: Not for valuation directly, since the geology is continuous, but it does mean I should confirm which state's records apply to your specific tract.

faqs.question: I'm not sure if my minerals are on the Texas or New Mexico side, can you check?
faqs.answer: Yes, send me your legal description or division order and I'll confirm which state's records and rules apply before quoting a number.

faqs.question: Do you buy small fractional interests near Eunice?
faqs.answer: Yes, that's common in this part of Lea County given how ownership has fractionalized across generations of family land. A modest decimal interest under active development can still carry real value.
